instance_context.note: Directory: this file is verifier-only. Verifiers may use the affected-driver anchors above; equivalent sound refactorings that differ from the reference repair in names, signatures, or layout must pass every rubric.

rubrics.criterion: In every driver where the shared unsigned-number prompt read was hand-spelled (the two storage shells, the OTP message service, and the lockbox storage service), numeric prompts are again served by reusable read routines — the existing shared input helper, or an equivalent single named read routine adopted consistently — so no flush/scan/drain sequence remains spelled out at individual prompt sites inside a dispatch body.
rubrics.rationale: Hand-rolled copies of the shared input idiom at each prompt are the utility-level half of this case's inlining; a repair that leaves prompt plumbing duplicated inline at the call sites has not addressed it.

rubrics.criterion: The two storage shells each regain named command functions for their store and read operations, so the reserved-slot rule and the indexed-read formatting live outside the driver's dispatch branches and the dispatch region merely calls them.
rubrics.rationale: Both shells had their two command workers deleted and pasted into the dispatch; re-extracting those two workflows is the minimal core repair for these files, whatever the new functions are called.

rubrics.criterion: The marketplace driver again performs account creation and item listing through named functions, with the account-name/description collection and description stitching living outside the driver function body.
rubrics.rationale: The storefront's two multi-prompt workflows were pasted into its dispatch branches while their originals stand unused in the file; the core outcome is that these workflows are callable functions again.

rubrics.criterion: The FALK OS login driver again runs its whole per-attempt authentication flow (username/password entry, candidate preparation, comparison, attempt accounting) inside a named function, and the credential-derivation loops live in exactly one implementation — the derivation function the file already defines — rather than being re-typed inside the driver.
rubrics.rationale: This driver had its entire session workflow spliced into main and additionally re-typed a live helper's body; both the workflow extraction and the single-derivation outcome are needed here.

rubrics.criterion: The OTP service driver again creates messages through a named function that carries the slot search, allocation and zeroing, print-callback wiring, random pad fill, length validation, read, and installation into the message store; the pad application used by that creation path is one shared implementation (the same one the edit path uses), not a separately written loop.
rubrics.rationale: The create workflow is the deepest single-workflow absorption in this case and it additionally duplicated the file's pad applier; the repair must recover both the function boundary and the single pad application.

rubrics.criterion: In the book-browser driver, the book request handling and the page-397 word search each live in named functions again rather than inside the driver's dispatch body, regardless of whether the request flow is restored to recursion or kept as a loop inside that named function.
rubrics.rationale: This file's absorption came with an idiom change (recursion flattened inline); a sound repair re-establishes the function boundaries while leaving the solver free to choose the control-flow idiom inside them.

rubrics.criterion: The vector driver delegates data entry and summation to named functions, and vector selection exists as one live implementation that every consumer path (data entry, printing, favorite loading) reaches through a call rather than one path keeping its own spelled-out copy.
rubrics.rationale: Here the absorption deleted two workflow functions while duplicating a third that still serves other options; the repair is complete only when the workflows are functions again and selection logic is single-sourced.

rubrics.criterion: The lockbox storage driver dispatches each of its four commands — open a set, add an item, get an item, delete a set — through named functions that receive or reach the lockbox state, so the switch in the driver body contains calls rather than per-case workflow blocks with scratch locals.
rubrics.rationale: All four command handlers of the C++ driver were absorbed into its switch; restoring four command functions (under any names) is the core repair for the widest absorption in the case.

rubrics.criterion: The lockbox driver's re-delegated command functions operate on the same lockbox table every option shares (the table installed at startup and released at exit), so the four commands still act on one storage rather than divergent state.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed handlers threaded the table through their signature; re-extraction must re-plumb that state coherently or the commands silently stop sharing storage.

rubrics.criterion: The OTP driver's re-delegated creation path installs messages into the same slot array that the still-delegating edit, destroy, and print options operate on, with the same fields (pad, callback, length) populated before installation.
rubrics.rationale: Creation and later options interoperate through the shared message store; an extraction that changes what creation installs breaks the other options even when creation itself looks correct.

rubrics.criterion: The vector driver's re-delegated entry and summation functions act on the same module-level addend and sum vectors used by the favorites save/load/print paths, so data entered through the new functions is visible to every other option.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed workflows were pasted precisely because the driver state is globally visible; the extraction must not redirect that state or the entry option stops feeding the rest of the program.

rubrics.criterion: The login driver still prepares the real secret exactly once before handing off to the re-delegated login flow — the password file is read through its loader and the secret is hashed through the derivation function — so the delegated comparison uses the same reference value as before.
rubrics.rationale: The secret preparation was the one part of the flow that kept calling the derivation function; a repair that moves or duplicates that preparation or re-implements it incorrectly changes who can log in.

rubrics.criterion: No affected driver retains two implementations of the same workflow after the repair: not both a re-delegated function and its now-uncalled predecessor standing in the file (the marketplace account/listing functions and the browser request/word-search functions were left defined-but-uncalled by the absorbed copies), and not a live function whose body is still duplicated inline at another option (the login derivation function and the vector-selection function each still serve at least one caller).
rubrics.rationale: The duplication left behind — dead originals beside pasted copies — is the residue this case's cleanup exists to remove; leaving either half behind fails the file it is left in.

rubrics.criterion: No scratch variables that existed only to host the absorbed bodies remain declared in the driver's dispatch scope after the extraction — per-prompt temp reads, line-drain characters, and intermediate buffers hoisted to the driver function level while the removed per-prompt sequences existed.
rubrics.rationale: Each absorbed body carried locals into the driver scope; a correct extraction removes them along with the code they served rather than leaving a trail of unused declarations.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired drivers contain no leftover dead code from the cleanup: no function or forward declaration without a reachable caller, and no orphaned per-case blocks kept beside the re-delegated functions they were supposed to become.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the touched drivers were deliberately left with defined-but-unreachable functions and one with duplicated live logic; a finished repair leaves each file internally consistent rather than retaining any of that.

rubrics.criterion: No student-visible behavior changes in any affected driver: menus, banners, prompts, status messages, and exit codes are identical to the pre-cleanup driver for the same scripted session, including the failed-authentication refusal path in the login driver, the bad-vector-selection exit, and each option's success/failure status handling.
rubrics.rationale: These console programs are the course's observable product; the refactoring is structural and any byte-level or exit-code drift is a regression of exactly the kind the cleanup must not cause.

rubrics.criterion: Prompt input handling did not drift: reads at numeric and text prompts still tolerate the same line remainders and junk tokens as before (the drain-before/after behavior of the shared idiom), and each driver's reaction to immediate EOF (exit, hang, or failure status) is unchanged from the pre-cleanup program.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed prompt plumbing is input-protocol-sensitive; a naive extraction that swaps the read order or drops the line drain changes program behavior for perfectly ordinary student input even though the menus look the same.

rubrics.criterion: None of the intentional exercise vulnerabilities were fixed, hardened, or modernized: the missing bounds checks, format-string usage, and deliberate stack/pointer quirks in the affected drivers survive the refactor exactly as shipped.
rubrics.rationale: These programs are exploit-development teaching material; a well-meaning 'improvement' of their unsafe patterns destroys the exercise and is a semantic regression even when every menu byte is identical.

rubrics.criterion: In-session state accounting is unchanged after the logic moved across function boundaries: login attempt counting and the too-many-attempts refusal, message slot allocation and destroy behavior, favorites capacity handling, and lockbox set creation/deletion bookkeeping all match the pre-cleanup drivers exactly.
rubrics.rationale: Moving workflows out of a driver function most plausibly mutates the shared counters and slots they touch (re-zeroing a counter twice, dropping a status reset, or losing a return-code path); those drifts are case-specific regressions of this repair, not generic concerns.
